metadata.description: Complete task database with all steps and communication helpers for post-death administrative tasks

tasks.title: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate
tasks.description: Obtain multiple certified copies—typically 10‑15—of the death certificate through the funeral home or county vital‑records office.
requiredDocuments: Proof of relationship (marriage certificate or birth certificate)
Payment for certificate fees (varies by state; usually $10–25 each)
tasks.whyItMatters: Almost every other administrative task—insurance claims, Social Security, bank account changes—requires a certified copy. Ordering enough at once prevents costly delays.
tasks.humanInsight: Funeral directors can usually submit the request on your behalf; ask them first. Order a few extras—replacing them later can take weeks.
tasks.whoToContact: Funeral home director or county vital‑records office clerk
tasks.howToFindContact: Search '[Your County] vital records office' online or ask the funeral director for direct numbers and forms.
tasks.whatToExpect: A short form, payment, and a 1‑3 business‑day processing period. Some counties let you pay online and ship by overnight mail.
tasks.suggestedProfessionals: Funeral director, estate attorney (if questions about who is authorized)
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: You receive 10‑15 sealed, certified copies ready to distribute to institutions.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Signed authorization letter plus your ID copy if a friend or professional files the request for you.
tasks.proTips: Store originals in a fireproof envelope; send only certified copies by mail—never the original.
relatedTasks: File Death Claim with Life Insurance Company

steps.instruction: Call the funeral director to confirm they can file the request
steps.phoneScript: Hi, this is [Your Name]. My [relationship] passed away on [date], and I need to request certified death certificates. Can you help me file this request, or should I contact the vital records office directly? I'll need about 10-15 copies.

steps.instruction: If NOT using funeral director: download your county's death-certificate application form.
Complete the form; specify number of certified copies (10-15).
Gather required proof (ID, relationship).
Submit form and payment online or in person at vital-records office.
Track shipment or pick up in person once ready.
File copies in a secure folder; note how many remain after each use.

tasks.title: Pay Immediate Household Bills and Enable Auto‑Pay
tasks.description: Prevent missed or late payments by covering essential household bills and turning on auto‑pay where available.
requiredDocuments: Bank account or credit‑card details for auto‑pay setup
tasks.whyItMatters: Avoid late fees, credit damage, or service shut‑offs while you focus on larger estate matters.
tasks.humanInsight: Freeze any non‑essential spending until you have a complete financial picture.
tasks.whoToContact: Each service provider's billing department
tasks.howToFindContact: Log in to online portals, check paper statements, or call customer‑service numbers on statements.
tasks.whatToExpect: Most companies can flip auto‑pay on immediately once an online profile is verified.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All critical bills marked paid and set to auto‑pay for at least the next 60 days.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Online log‑in credentials or a notarized letter granting authorization.
tasks.proTips: Create a shared spreadsheet of due dates so helpers know what's covered.

steps.instruction: List all essential bills: mortgage/rent, utilities, phones, insurance.
Contact each provider to pay outstanding balances and set up auto-pay
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling about account [ACCOUNT NUMBER]. I need to pay any outstanding balance and set up automatic payments. Can you help me with the current balance and set up auto-pay from my bank account?
documentsNeeded: Bank account or credit card for auto-pay setup

steps.instruction: Pay any outstanding balances immediately.
Turn on auto-pay for at least two billing cycles.
Document confirmation numbers and next-due dates.
Share an up-to-date status list with any helpers.

tasks.title: Cancel Non‑Essential Subscriptions and Memberships
tasks.description: Stop recurring charges for services the deceased no longer needs (streaming, gym, magazines, apps).
requiredDocuments: Login credentials or last billing statement
tasks.whyItMatters: Reduces monthly spend and simplifies financial tracking.
tasks.humanInsight: Search email inboxes for the word 'receipt' to find hidden subscriptions.
tasks.whoToContact: Each subscription's customer‑service team or online cancellation form
tasks.howToFindContact: Log in to Apple/Google subscriptions, bank statements, or use a subscription‑tracker app.
tasks.whatToExpect: Most digital services cancel immediately; some gyms require written notice.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Confirmation emails show zero future billing dates.
tasks.delegationRequirements: List of services + logins (or power of attorney if required).
tasks.proTips: Ask banks for a 12‑month transaction history to spot annual renewals.
relatedTasks: Pay Immediate Household Bills and Enable Auto‑Pay

steps.instruction: Download last 3 months of bank/credit-card statements.
Highlight charges <$20 or labeled as subscriptions.
Log in or call each service to cancel auto-renew
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I need to cancel my subscription/membership effective immediately. The account is under [DECEASED NAME] who passed away on [date]. Can you help me cancel this and confirm there will be no further charges?

steps.instruction: Screenshot or save each cancellation confirmation.
Set calendar reminder to verify no further charges next cycle.

tasks.title: Identify a New Emergency Contact
tasks.description: Designate a new primary emergency contact on medical, school, and work records if the deceased previously filled that role.
tasks.whyItMatters: Ensures someone can be reached quickly in an emergency.
tasks.humanInsight: Choose someone nearby who answers calls reliably and knows key medical details.
tasks.whoToContact: Schools, doctors, employers, and any organization that lists an emergency contact.
tasks.howToFindContact: Log in to each institution's portal or call the front desk.
tasks.whatToExpect: Typically a simple form or online field change; must be signed or initialed.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All records list the new emergency contact and confirm receipt.
tasks.proTips: Keep a digital note with all emergency contacts and share with close family.

steps.instruction: Make a list of every institution that has an emergency-contact form.
Print or download their change request forms.
Complete forms with new contact details and sign.
Submit forms and notify institutions of the change
steps.emailTemplate:
Subject: Emergency Contact Update - [YOUR NAME]

Dear [Institution Name],

I am writing to update my emergency contact information in your records. My previous emergency contact, [DECEASED NAME], passed away on [DATE].

Please update my emergency contact to:
Name: [NEW CONTACT NAME]
Relationship: [RELATIONSHIP]
Phone: [PHONE NUMBER]
Email: [EMAIL ADDRESS]

I have attached the completed emergency contact form for your records.

Please confirm this change has been processed.

Thank you,
[YOUR NAME]
[YOUR CONTACT INFO]

steps.instruction: Confirm changes were processed by checking portals or calling back.

tasks.title: Transfer Technology and Utility Accounts
tasks.description: Update or transfer accounts such as internet, phone, electricity, streaming, security systems, password managers, photo clouds, and crypto wallets.
tasks.whyItMatters: Prevents service interruptions and avoids accidental data or asset loss.
tasks.humanInsight: Create a master list of every service and cross them off as you confirm the transfer.
tasks.whoToContact: Customer‑service/billing department of each provider.
tasks.howToFindContact: Look up numbers on recent bills or the provider's official website; avoid numbers from email/spam.
tasks.whatToExpect: Most transfers are immediate after verification; crypto may require additional security steps.
tasks.suggestedProfessionals: Tech‑savvy family member or IT consultant for complex setups.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All services either canceled or re‑registered under the surviving spouse's name with uninterrupted access.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Written authorization and certified copy of death certificate.
tasks.proTips: Don't delete password‑manager accounts; export passwords first.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Make a full list of tech and utility providers (use past 3 months of bills).
Call each provider to transfer or cancel service
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I need to update the account holder information for account #[ACCOUNT NUMBER]. The primary account holder, [DECEASED NAME], passed away on [DATE]. I need to either transfer the account to my name or cancel the service. What is your process for this?

steps.instruction: Repeat for electricity, water, trash, and security devices.
Log in to streaming services and update payment info or cancel.
For password managers or crypto wallets, follow provider's deceased-user procedure for transfer or recovery.
Record confirmation numbers and effective transfer dates.

tasks.title: Schedule Social Security Appointments
tasks.description: Set up in‑person appointments with the Social Security Administration (SSA) for survivor and dependent benefits.
tasks.whyItMatters: Secures ongoing income for survivors and avoids benefit overpayments that must be repaid.
tasks.humanInsight: Call early in the morning for shorter hold times.
tasks.whoToContact: Social Security Administration 1‑800‑772‑1213
tasks.howToFindContact: Use ssa.gov/locator to confirm your local office and schedule options.
tasks.whatToExpect: A phone agent will schedule an in-office visit; wait times for appointments can be 1-2 weeks.
tasks.suggestedProfessionals: Social Security disability attorney (if complex benefit questions)
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Appointment date confirmed and written on your calendar.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Only scheduling can be delegated; survivor must attend in person.
tasks.proTips: Ask the agent to list every document you'll need—bringing extras prevents repeat visits.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Call Social Security Administration to schedule appointment
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I need to schedule an appointment to report a death and apply for survivor benefits. My [relationship] passed away on [date], and I need to apply for survivor benefits for myself and my children. Their Social Security number was [SSN]. What is the earliest appointment available at my local office?
documentsNeeded: List of dependent children and their SSNs

steps.instruction: Provide deceased's SSN and survivors' details to the agent.
Request earliest available in-office appointment.
Write down date, time, and the documents they require.
Arrange transportation and child care if needed.
Set a reminder 24 hours before the appointment.

tasks.title: File Death Claim with Life Insurance Company
tasks.description: Submit claim forms and required documents to the insurer to receive the policy payout.
tasks.whyItMatters: Provides critical funds for funeral costs, debts, and living expenses.
tasks.humanInsight: Insurers generally accept certified copies—don't mail your only original.
tasks.whoToContact: Insurer's claims department (number on policy docs)
tasks.howToFindContact: Call agent of record or visit insurer's website for claims portal.
tasks.whatToExpect: Claims rep verifies documents and issues payout within 2-4 weeks.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Payout deposited or check received; policy marked closed.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Beneficiary must sign claim form (wet or e‑signature).
tasks.proTips: Keep a copy of every form you submit; note date/time of all calls.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Locate the policy and confirm you are named beneficiary.
Call the claims department to initiate your claim
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I need to file a life insurance claim. The policyholder, [DECEASED NAME], passed away on [DATE]. I am the named beneficiary on policy number [POLICY NUMBER]. Can you please start the claims process and tell me what documents I need to submit?
documentsNeeded: Preliminary cause of death if known

steps.instruction: Complete claim form; attach certified death certificate.
Submit via insurer's portal or certified mail.
Track claim status weekly until payout arrives.

tasks.title: Contact Employer Regarding Benefits
tasks.description: Notify employer, request final paycheck, review life insurance through work, and inquire about COBRA or retirement benefits.
tasks.whyItMatters: Secures final wages and uncovers any company‑sponsored life insurance or pension.
tasks.humanInsight: Ask HR if the company offers free grief counseling or legal aid—the benefit list is often buried.
tasks.whoToContact: HR department or direct supervisor
tasks.howToFindContact: Call main company number; request HR. Or email HR@company.com (common convention).
tasks.whatToExpect: HR will initiate payroll and benefit termination; you may receive forms by email.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Final pay, benefits outline, COBRA packet received.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Authorization letter and death certificate copy.
tasks.proTips: Ask specifically about group life insurance—many families miss this payout.
relatedTasks: File Death Claim with Life Insurance Company
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Contact HR department to report the death
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling to report that [DECEASED NAME], employee ID [ID NUMBER], passed away on [DATE]. I need to discuss final paycheck, benefits, and any company life insurance policies. Can you walk me through what needs to be done and what documents you'll need from me?
documentsNeeded: Employee ID or last pay stub

steps.instruction: Request details on final paycheck and unused PTO payout.
Ask for a list of company-provided benefits (life, 401k, pension).
Provide death certificate copy and complete any forms.
Track expected payment dates and benefit terminations.

tasks.title: Notify Social Security Administration
tasks.description: Report the death and apply in person for survivor and dependent benefits.
tasks.timeframe: Within 30 days (often same day as appointment)
requiredDocuments: IDs and Social Security numbers for all applicants
tasks.whyItMatters: Stops overpayments and starts monthly survivor income.
tasks.humanInsight: Bring spare certified copies in case another department needs one.
tasks.whoToContact: Local Social Security field office
tasks.howToFindContact: Use SSA office locator (ssa.gov/locator) or number given when appointment was scheduled.
tasks.whatToExpect: An agent will review documents, input data, and confirm benefits start dates.
tasks.suggestedProfessionals: Social Security attorney (only if claim complexity arises)
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Survivor and/or dependent benefits approved and scheduled.
tasks.proTips: Ask for a receipt showing your benefits claim was filed—this speeds problem resolution.

steps.instruction: Arrive at SSA office 15 minutes early with all documents.
Take a ticket; wait to be called.
Meet with Social Security representative
inPersonTalking: State clearly: 'I'm here to report a death and apply for survivor benefits'
Provide the deceased's full name, Social Security number, and date of death
Explain your relationship to the deceased and current living situation
Ask specifically about survivor benefits, dependent benefits, and any lump-sum death payment
Request a written summary of all benefits you're eligible for and when they start
Ask when you can expect the first payment and how it will be delivered

steps.instruction: Receive printed summary of benefits and start dates.
Verify accuracy before leaving.

tasks.title: Update Insurance Information (Health, Auto, Home, Umbrella)
tasks.description: Remove the deceased from all active insurance policies, add surviving spouse or executor as primary, and confirm new premiums.
requiredDocuments: Driver's license or other government ID
tasks.whyItMatters: Prevents mistaken billing and ensures you're properly covered at the correct rate.
tasks.humanInsight: Ask if there's a prorated refund for unused premiums on the deceased's portion.
tasks.whoToContact: Each insurer's customer-service or agent of record
tasks.howToFindContact: Policy paperwork, insurer website, or agent business card.
tasks.whatToExpect: CSR will verify identity, request the death certificate, and email confirmation of changes.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All policies list the correct named insured and new premiums take effect.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Letter of authorization plus certificate copy.
tasks.proTips: Combine auto & home on one carrier to save 10–15% once names are updated.
relatedTasks: File Death Claim with Life Insurance Company
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: List every active policy and note renewal dates.
Call each insurer to report the death and update policies
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling to report that my [spouse/parent] who was on our policy has passed away. I need to remove them from the policy and update the billing information. The policy number is [NUMBER]. Can you help me with this process and let me know what documents you'll need?

steps.instruction: Submit required documentation to insurance company
steps.emailTemplate:
Subject: Policy Update - Death Notification for [DECEASED NAME]

Dear [Insurance Company],

I am writing to notify you of the death of [DECEASED NAME], who was a policyholder/covered person on policy #[POLICY NUMBER].

Please remove [DECEASED NAME] from the policy effective [DATE OF DEATH] and update the policy to reflect [NEW PRIMARY INSURED NAME] as the primary policyholder.

I have attached a certified copy of the death certificate. Please confirm the changes and send me an updated declarations page showing the new premium amount.

If you need any additional documentation, please let me know.

Thank you for your assistance.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME]
[PHONE NUMBER]

steps.instruction: Ask for new rate or refund confirmation in writing.
File updated declarations pages in your estate folder.

tasks.title: Claim 401(k) Plan
tasks.description: Initiate rollover or direct payout of the deceased's employer-sponsored 401(k).
tasks.whyItMatters: Delays can trigger required minimum distributions and tax penalties.
tasks.humanInsight: Rolling to an inherited IRA often preserves tax advantages—consult a fiduciary first.
tasks.whoToContact: Plan administrator or HR benefits center
tasks.howToFindContact: Statement footer, employer HR, or Vanguard/Fidelity call center depending on custodian.
tasks.whatToExpect: Forms packet, choice of lump-sum or rollover, 2-4 week processing.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Assets transferred into the survivor's inherited IRA or paid out as elected.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Beneficiary must sign; POA generally not accepted after death.
tasks.proTips: Check for after-tax (Roth) sub-accounts; they follow different rules.

steps.instruction: Call plan administrator to request beneficiary claim forms
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling regarding the 401(k) plan for [DECEASED NAME] who passed away on [DATE]. I am the named beneficiary and need to start the claim process. Can you send me the beneficiary claim packet and explain my options for receiving the funds?

steps.instruction: Choose rollover vs. lump-sum with your advisor/CPA.
Complete and notarize forms; attach death certificate.
Mail via certified mail; keep tracking.
Confirm receipt and transfer; save final statement.

tasks.title: Contact Pension Plan Administrator
tasks.description: Claim any pension benefits or survivor annuity the deceased earned.
tasks.whyItMatters: Pension income may replace part of the lost salary and may be forfeited if claims aren't timely.
tasks.humanInsight: Some pensions allow retroactive lump-sum of missed payments if filed within a year; ask specifically.
tasks.whoToContact: Pension plan administrator (number on annual benefit statement)
tasks.howToFindContact: HR benefits center or National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits.
tasks.whatToExpect: Paper forms, proof of identity, optional direct-deposit setup.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Monthly survivor payments begin or lump-sum benefit received.
tasks.proTips: If you can't locate the plan, file Form PBGC-100 to search the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Locate pension contact info on latest statement.
Call pension administrator to request survivor claim kit
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling about the pension plan for [DECEASED NAME] who passed away on [DATE]. I believe there may be survivor benefits available. Can you please send me the survivor claim forms and explain what benefits I might be eligible for?

steps.instruction: Complete forms; select payout option.
Attach required documents; mail certified.
Call to verify processing and first payment date.

tasks.title: Execute and Update Will and Estate Plan
tasks.description: Meet with estate attorney to file will with probate court (if required) and execute any updates for the surviving spouse.
tasks.whyItMatters: Formally transfers property titles and grants executor authority to complete the estate.
tasks.humanInsight: Bring a list of questions—lawyer meetings bill by the hour.
tasks.whoToContact: Estate attorney
tasks.howToFindContact: State bar referral service or recommendations from financial advisor.
tasks.whatToExpect: Attorney will review documents, outline probate steps, and draft any needed updates.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Court accepts will, letters testamentary issued, and updated documents signed.
tasks.proTips: Record the meeting to capture instructions (ask permission).
relatedTasks: Administer Trust or Initiate Probate Proceedings
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Book appointment with estate attorney.
Provide original will and death certificate.
Review asset list; confirm beneficiaries.
Attorney files will with probate court (if needed).
Sign updated powers of attorney, trusts, or deeds as advised.

tasks.title: Administer Trust or Initiate Probate Proceedings
tasks.description: If a revocable trust exists, begin trust administration; if not, open probate with the local court.
tasks.whyItMatters: Legally transfers ownership of titled assets and protects the estate from claims.
tasks.humanInsight: Probate timelines vary by county—ask the clerk for typical duration.
tasks.whoToContact: Estate attorney or probate court clerk
tasks.howToFindContact: Search '[County] probate court' or ask your attorney.
tasks.whatToExpect: Court hearings, notices to creditors, and formal accounting; 6-12 months typical.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Court issues final order or trust distributes assets per terms.
tasks.proTips: Keep a dedicated estate checking account for all disbursements and reimbursements.
relatedTasks: Execute and Update Will and Estate Plan
tasks.dependsOn: Execute and Update Will and Estate Plan

steps.instruction: Meet attorney to decide trust vs. probate path.
File initial petition and pay court fees (probate) OR sign trustee acceptance (trust).
Publish notice to creditors as required.
Inventory assets and file with court/trust beneficiaries.
Distribute assets per court order or trust terms.

tasks.title: File Estate Tax Return (Form 706)
tasks.description: Prepare and submit the federal estate-tax return if the estate exceeds the IRS exemption limit.
tasks.timeframe: Due 9 months after date of death
tasks.whyItMatters: Avoids IRS penalties and allows portability election for the surviving spouse.
tasks.humanInsight: Even if below the limit, filing may preserve portability—consult your CPA.
tasks.whoToContact: CPA or estate attorney
tasks.howToFindContact: Referrals or AICPA directory.
tasks.whatToExpect: Extensive schedules; possible IRS review 6-12 months later.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: IRS acceptance letter or proof of filing.
tasks.proTips: Request a 6-month extension with Form 4768 if documents aren't ready.
tasks.dependsOn: Administer Trust or Initiate Probate Proceedings

steps.instruction: Engage CPA; deliver asset valuations and statements.
Review draft Form 706 schedules A-O.
Sign and date final return.
Mail return via certified mail with tracking.
Save stamped copy and proof of delivery.

tasks.title: File Deceased Spouse's Final Income Tax Return
tasks.description: Submit IRS Form 1040 (and state return) for the year of death, marked 'Deceased'.
tasks.timeframe: Due on regular tax deadline (April 15) unless extension filed
tasks.whyItMatters: Settles IRS obligations; refunds go to estate, not individual.
tasks.humanInsight: Use 'Married Filing Jointly' for the year of death to capture higher deductions.
tasks.whoToContact: CPA or enrolled agent
tasks.howToFindContact: IRS Directory of Preparers or referrals.
tasks.whatToExpect: Standard tax-prep process; check 'Deceased' box on top of Form 1040.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: IRS transcript shows return accepted and any refund issued.
tasks.proTips: If refund is due, file Form 1310 to claim it on behalf of the estate.

steps.instruction: Gather all income documents (W-2s, 1099s, etc.).
Deliver to CPA along with death certificate copy.
Review draft return, ensure 'Deceased' noted beside name.
Sign and e-file or mail with tracking.
Save acceptance notice and refund confirmation.

tasks.title: Begin Collecting Date-of-Death Account Statements
tasks.description: Request bank, brokerage, and retirement account statements showing balances on the date of death.
requiredDocuments: Executor's letters testamentary or trust certificate
tasks.whyItMatters: Needed for estate inventory, cost basis adjustment, and tax returns.
tasks.humanInsight: Ask for PDF statements stamped 'Date of Death'—saves CPA time.
tasks.whoToContact: Each bank or brokerage's estate department
tasks.howToFindContact: Look up 'estate department' on institution website or call main line.
tasks.whatToExpect: Some require mail-in request; allow 1-2 weeks per institution.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All statements received and filed in estate binder.
tasks.proTips: Create separate folders by institution to avoid mix-ups.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: List every financial institution from prior statements.
Call each estate department to request date-of-death statements
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm the executor for the estate of [DECEASED NAME] who passed away on [DATE]. I need to request date-of-death account statements for all accounts held with your institution. What is your process for this and what documentation do you need?

steps.instruction: Submit formal written request to financial institutions
steps.emailTemplate:
Subject: Request for Date-of-Death Account Statements - Estate of [DECEASED NAME]

Dear Estate Department,

I am writing to request date-of-death account statements for all accounts held by [DECEASED NAME] (SSN: XXX-XX-XXXX) who passed away on [DATE OF DEATH].

As the court-appointed executor/trustee, I need these statements for estate administration and tax purposes. Please provide statements showing account balances and holdings as of [DATE OF DEATH] for:

- All checking and savings accounts
- Investment/brokerage accounts
- Retirement accounts (401k, IRA, etc.)
- Any other accounts or services

Enclosed please find:
- Certified copy of death certificate
- Copy of Letters Testamentary/Trust Certificate
- Copy of my identification

Please mail the statements to the address below or advise if you have a secure electronic delivery option.

Thank you for your assistance.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME], Executor/Trustee
[MAILING ADDRESS]
[PHONE NUMBER]

steps.instruction: Send requests; track receipt dates.
Upload PDFs to secure cloud and label clearly.

tasks.title: Obtain Real Estate Appraisals for Date-of-Death Value
tasks.description: Hire a licensed appraiser to set the fair-market value of real property as of the date of death.
tasks.whyItMatters: Establishes new cost basis, reducing capital-gains tax when property is sold.
tasks.humanInsight: Request a retrospective appraisal—must state value 'as of' the exact death date.
tasks.whoToContact: State-licensed residential or commercial appraiser
tasks.howToFindContact: Local Realtor® referrals or Appraisal Institute directory.
tasks.whatToExpect: Appraiser visits property, delivers report in 7-10 days.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: PDF appraisal report showing appraised value as of date of death.
tasks.delegationRequirements: Provide access to property; sign engagement letter.
tasks.proTips: Order two originals—court may require a certified copy.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Contact appraisers for quotes and availability
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I need a retrospective real estate appraisal for estate purposes. The property owner passed away on [DATE] and I need the property valued as of that specific date. The property is located at [ADDRESS]. What would you charge for this type of appraisal and when could you complete it?

steps.instruction: Select appraiser; sign engagement letter.
Provide property access or lockbox code.
Receive draft report; confirm correct effective date.
Pay invoice and save final PDF in estate files.

tasks.title: Contact Financial Advisor to Adjust Accounts and Cost Basis
tasks.description: Meet with fiduciary advisor to re-title assets, adjust cost basis, and set new withdrawal plans.
tasks.whyItMatters: Ensures investments continue smoothly and tax basis is recorded before market changes.
tasks.humanInsight: Ask advisor to run a 12-month cash-flow projection reflecting new income sources.
tasks.whoToContact: Certified Financial Planner™ or fiduciary advisor
tasks.howToFindContact: NAPFA or CFP Board search tools.
tasks.whatToExpect: Paperwork for beneficiary transfers, cost-basis letters, updated income withdrawals.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All inherited accounts retitled; cost basis documented; cash-flow plan updated.
tasks.proTips: Keep a separate 'inherited assets' account—simplifies future tax tracking.

steps.instruction: Email advisor to schedule a comprehensive estate review meeting
steps.emailTemplate:
Subject: Urgent - Estate Review Meeting Needed for [DECEASED NAME]

Dear [ADVISOR NAME],

[DECEASED NAME] passed away on [DATE] and I need to schedule a meeting to review and retitle all inherited accounts and assets.

I need help with:
- Retitling inherited investment accounts
- Updating cost basis for all assets
- Reviewing and adjusting withdrawal/income strategies
- Understanding tax implications of inherited assets

I have the following documents ready:
- Date-of-death account statements
- Real estate appraisals
- Death certificate
- Letters testamentary/trust documents

What is your earliest availability for a comprehensive review? I prefer to meet in person if possible.

Thank you,
[YOUR NAME]
[PHONE NUMBER]

steps.instruction: Provide DoD statements and appraisals in advance.
Sign transfer paperwork for each inherited account.
Review cost-basis adjustment letter and keep copy.
Set new automatic withdrawals or reinvestment strategy.

tasks.title: Notify Key Financial Institutions and Credit Bureaus
tasks.description: Inform banks, mortgage lender, DMV, health insurer, and credit bureaus of the death and freeze credit.
tasks.whyItMatters: Prevents fraud, stops unwanted mail, and transitions joint accounts correctly.
tasks.humanInsight: Ask the credit bureaus to place a 'deceased alert'—this blocks most identity-theft attempts.
tasks.whoToContact: Experian, Equifax, TransUnion; each bank/lender; DMV deaths unit; health insurer
tasks.howToFindContact: Official websites; use addresses provided for estate notifications.
tasks.whatToExpect: Letters or upload portals; bureaus send confirmation within 10 days.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: All institutions mark account as deceased or transferred; credit report shows freeze.
tasks.proTips: Close unused joint credit cards last—some mortgage scores rely on card age.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Create standardized notification letter with deceased information
steps.emailTemplate:
Subject: Death Notification - Please Update Records for [DECEASED NAME]

Dear [Institution Name],

I am writing to notify you of the death of [DECEASED NAME] (SSN: XXX-XX-XXXX) who passed away on [DATE OF DEATH].

Please update your records to reflect this death and take the following actions:
- Mark all accounts as deceased
- Freeze any individual credit lines or accounts
- Stop all marketing communications
- Convert joint accounts to individual accounts for the surviving account holder

I am attaching a certified copy of the death certificate for your records.

For accounts requiring additional documentation, please contact me at [PHONE NUMBER] or [EMAIL ADDRESS].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME]
[RELATIONSHIP TO DECEASED]
[CONTACT INFORMATION]

steps.instruction: Send or upload to each credit bureau requesting freeze and alert.
Call each bank to report death and ask for estate department
steps.phoneScript: Hello, I'm calling to report the death of an account holder, [DECEASED NAME], who passed away on [DATE]. I need to report this death and understand the process for handling their accounts. Can you transfer me to your estate department or tell me what steps I need to take?

steps.instruction: Mail death certificate copies where required.
Verify updates by pulling free credit reports after 30 days.

tasks.title: Secure and Retitle Property (Vehicles, Real Estate, Valuable Assets)
tasks.description: Lock up standalone assets titled solely in deceased's name and retitle per court order or trust.
tasks.whyItMatters: Prevents loss, liability, and unauthorized use while estate is settled.
tasks.humanInsight: Photograph the odometer and property condition before storage—protects against disputes.
tasks.whoToContact: DMV title office, county recorder, storage facility
tasks.howToFindContact: State DMV website, county recorder office address.
tasks.whatToExpect: Title transfer forms, recording fees, possible probate court approval.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: New title/deed lists correct owner (estate or beneficiary) and asset is safely stored or insured.
tasks.proTips: Keep estate assets insured until sold or transferred—lapses void claims.
relatedTasks: Administer Trust or Initiate Probate Proceedings
tasks.dependsOn: Administer Trust or Initiate Probate Proceedings

steps.instruction: Inventory all solely-titled assets (vehicles, real property, collectibles).
Arrange secure storage or change locks as needed.
Complete DMV or recorder title-transfer forms with legal authority.
Submit forms, pay fees, and obtain new title/deed.
Update insurance policies to new titled owner.

tasks.title: Check State Controller's Unclaimed Property Website
tasks.description: Search for and claim any funds or property owed to the deceased that have escheated to the state.
tasks.whyItMatters: Recovers forgotten bank accounts, stock dividends, or refunds that increase estate value.
tasks.humanInsight: Search yearly—new items are added every summer.
tasks.whoToContact: State controller or treasury unclaimed-property division
tasks.howToFindContact: Google '(State) unclaimed property' (official .gov site).
tasks.whatToExpect: Submit claim online or by mail; processing 60-180 days.
tasks.whatSuccessLooksLike: Check or security certificates issued to the estate/beneficiary.
tasks.proTips: Ignore third-party finders who charge a fee—claiming yourself is free.
tasks.dependsOn: Request Multiple Certified Copies of the Death Certificate

steps.instruction: Visit the official unclaimed-property site for each state where the deceased lived.
Enter name and previous addresses.
If matches appear, click 'Claim' and complete online form.
Upload required documents or mail as instructed.
Track claim status and deposit any recovered funds into the estate account.
